subject: Re: Cross-account peering -> misrouted returns + MTU/ephemeral port failures
messages:
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@finedge.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@finedge.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Connectivity: intermittent TLS failures for private deployment

Jonas,

We started seeing intermittent TLS connection failures between our on-prem app stack and the Redwood private endpoints hosted in our VPC (account: 111122223333). Symptoms: approx 2-3% of API calls fail with TLS handshake errors or TCP RSTs during the hour windows noted below. The failures are reproducible from our datacenter behind the IPsec VPN.

What we've observed so far:
- 2026-10-10 08:05-09:20 PDT: spike of application errors; logs show TLS handshake timeouts and 'connection reset by peer'.
- tcpdump on our edge (attached: pcap snippet) shows ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages and some SYN/ACKs coming from unexpected public IPs.
- No recent config changes on our side aside from a scheduled ASN announcement change last week.

We suspect either MTU/tunnel fragmentation issues or some return-path asymmetry (packets are being SNATed to a different account's NAT). Can you help triage? We're happy to run commands you need.

Attachments: finedge_pcap_snippet.txt (small tcpdump extract)

Thanks,
Alex
NetOps Lead, FinEdge

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@finedge.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@finedge.com>, dev_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Connectivity: intermittent TLS failures for private deployment

Alex — thanks for the details and the pcap. We’ll take point on this. Quick ask to help speed debugging: please share (or run) the following and paste results:

1) traceroute (ICMP & TCP) from your edge to the Redwood endpoint IP (both short and long pings).
2) iptables/nat rules on your VPN gateway (if any) and whether you have an intermediate NAT in your on-prem path.
3) output of 'ip -s link' to show MTU on the tunnel, and 'show route' from your edge (to confirm learned prefixes).
4) Any AWS account IDs or TGW attachment IDs we should look up; you pasted 111122223333 but if there are multiple accounts in your org list them.

Internal: looping in @dev_patel for routing/TGW, @marissa_cole for VPC peering/NAT analysis, and @hannah_schmitt for on-prem VPN/MTU guidance. I've attached our Redwood troubleshooting checklist to make sure we cover standard items.

Next steps from our side: we'll pull TGW/route table state, check for overlapping prefixes propagated from your account to any partner account, and confirm whether any NAT Gateway in our environment is seeing traffic from your IPs (which would indicate SNAT).

— Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_troubleshooting_checklist.pdf

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Kim <alex.kim@finedge.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@finedge.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Connectivity: intermittent TLS failures for private deployment

Team / Alex — did a first-pass on routing and NAT: findings below (commands and screenshots attached). Summary: asymmetric return-path caused by cross-account TGW route propagation + a NAT in Account 444455556666 performing SNAT, combined with VPN MTU mismatch.

What I looked at:
- TGW route tables (all attachments): found overlapping 10.20.0.0/16 learned from FinEdge account (111122223333) and a more-specific 10.20.128.0/18 learned from Partner account (444455556666). TGW will prefer the more-specific route — traffic egressed to the partner account attachment for certain subnets.
- Flow logs & NAT logs: some flows from FinEdge source IPs are being NATed to an EIP belonging to 444455556666 (NAT Gateway). That explains the unexpected public IPs in the capture. Return traffic is going to the NAT EIP which doesn't know how to forward back to the VPN tunnel -> RSTs and handshake failures.
- MTU: The IPsec tunnel on FinEdge side is 1400 MTU, while the TGW/VPN path is currently seeing ~1500. Fragmentation-needed ICMPs were observed; we also saw TLS with MSS clamping needed.
- Security groups: Redwood side had a rule set that limited ephemeral port range to 49152-65535 on one interface, while the partner NAT instance was translating to ports outside that range in some flows — so some replies were dropped.

Immediate mitigations (short window) — what we recommend now:
1) Add an explicit route on TGW route-table for the affected subnets 10.20.0.0/16 pointing to the FinEdge attachment to override the more-specific learned route from the partner. This is a stop-gap to force symmetric pathing.
2) Replace the partner NAT gateway in 444455556666 with a NAT instance or configure 1:1 mapping so SNAT doesn't happen for FinEdge source ranges, or modify that account's route propagation to avoid taking precedence.
3) On the FinEdge VPN device, enable TCP MSS clamping to 1360 (or adjust to match 1400 MTU) and enable PMTUD logs.
4) Amend Redwood security group to widen ephemeral port acceptance temporarily (1024-65535) on the interface with the TGW attachment until NAT mappings settle.

Longer-term fixes:
- Clean up overlapping prefixes across partners; encourage unique subnet slices per partner account or use TGW route filters to block propagation of the conflicting 10.20.128.0/18.
- Add TGW route propagation guards and more specific route advertisements from FinEdge to prevent partner hijack.
- Consider using a Transit VPC pattern with SRv6/VRF separation for customer isolation.

Attached: route-table-screenshot.png showing the conflicting learned routes, and command outputs that show NAT EIP mappings.

I'll hold on any changes until Alex confirms we can perform the TGW route override and security group expansion. If FinEdge prefers, we can coordinate with AWS Support to perform a controlled NAT replacement in the partner account.

— Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@finedge.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@finedge.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Connectivity: intermittent TLS failures for private deployment

Team — quick update and confirmation: we implemented the TGW route override (pointed 10.20.0.0/16 back to our FinEdge attachment), requested the partner to remove the conflicting 10.20.128.0/18 advertisement, and AWS Support replaced the partner NAT with a NAT instance configured for 1:1 mappings. On our side we enabled MSS clamp to 1360 and widened the ephemeral port range during the window.

Result: TLS handshake failures dropped to <0.1% during the monitored window; packet captures look clean and there are no more SYN/ACKs coming from unexpected EIPs.

Thanks to @dev_patel and @marissa_cole for leading the network fixes and to Redwood for coordinating with AWS. We'll keep the wider ephemeral port rule for 48 hours for monitoring and will revert if no regressions.

I'll open a change request internally to clean up subnet overlap in our org and will supply the final post-mortem once we've validated for 72 hours.

— Alex
NetOps Lead, FinEdge
